title: @skills: Attention is all you have
abstract: arXiv:2608.12610v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: There are 56,804 public agent skills today, and teams write many more privately. The dominant delivery model is installation: once installed, a skill's description remains in the system prompt, competing for fewer than 100 reliable trigger slots. This leaves the long tail with no practical path to use and forces teams' own playbooks to compete for the same scarce space. We observe that installation bundles three separable functions: content, persistence, and automatic triggering. Only the last requires prompt residency. We therefore propose @skills, an open protocol that separates them. A path addresses any skill, subtree, or collection, and reading a skill is sufficient to use it, so nothing is installed or made resident. The operation vendors a copy at the same path into a project's Git-tracked tree for adaptation and ownership. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12610v1 公告类型：新 摘要：目前有56,804个公开的智能体技能，且团队还私下编写了更多。主导的交付模式是安装：一旦安装，技能描述会保留在系统提示中，争夺不到100个可靠的触发槽位。这使得长尾技能没有实际使用路径，并迫使团队自己的操作手册竞争同一稀缺空间。我们观察到，安装将三个可分离的功能捆绑在一起：内容、持久性和自动触发。只有最后一项需要提示词驻留。因此，我们提出@技能，一个将它们分离的开放协议。一个路径可指向任何技能、子树或集合，读取一个技能就足以使用它，因此无需安装或驻留。操作将同一路径下的副本供应商到项目的Git跟踪树中，以供适配和所有权管理。该操作添加一行.gitignore风格的行，这是唯一需要提示词驻留的要素。一个目录即是...
tldr: 本文提出@skills协议，将技能安装中的内容、持久性和自动触发功能分离，仅保留触发所需的最小提示词驻留，从而解决长尾技能无法使用和系统提示空间稀缺的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the @skills protocol that separates content, persistence, and automatic triggering in skill installation, retaining only the minimal prompt residency for triggering, thereby addressing the impracticality of long-tail skills and the scarcity of system prompt space.
